event: Nala says, "Yes, it sounds like poison is the best option to improve our chances."
"We could poison the heads of the spears as well as the stakes."
"I will come, and I will pray for your success."

changes.note: Tie Bo +5: she kept to the hunt, heard him, shared a plan for poison, and offered prayer

memory.fact: She urged poisoning the stakes and the heads of the spears, and said she would pray for Tie Bo.
She urged poisoning the stakes and the heads of the spears, and said she would pray for Tie Bo.
She urged poisoning the stakes and the heads of the spears, and said she would pray for Tie Bo.
Nala agreed to come to the hunt and keep behind the stakes, out of the line.

event: Tie Bo nods slowly. "Then I'll ask her at first light."

memory.fact: Tie Bo said he would ask Granny Hua for the poison at first light.
Tie Bo said he would ask Granny Hua for the poison at first light.

event: He is quiet a moment, and then he says the rest of it, because she should hear it from him.
"Poison on a spirit beast, though. The old tales say it's no use."
"They say a poisoned bait kills the village dogs, and the beast goes on eating."

memory.fact: Tales warn that a poisoned bait kills the village dogs and no spirit beast.
Tales warn that a poisoned bait kills the village dogs and no spirit beast.

event: "But it's worth the trying, and I'll take it if she gives it."
"I'll smear the heads too, if there's enough. Poison or no poison, we go up after it."
"The stakes and the men I'd be sure of, whether there's poison or not."
He shoulders his bow. "And I'll not pretend to you. It's my brother's boar."
"I'd go up that hill with a spear and no plan at all, if that were all I had."

memory.fact: Tie Bo would go up after the boar with a spear and no plan at all, if that were all he had.
Tie Bo would go up after the boar with a spear and no plan at all, if that were all he had.

event: They walk back up the dark track to the headman's gate. The lamp is still burning inside.
Zhao Jun comes out, and his eyes are red, and he stops in front of Nala and bows.
"Thank you, honored spirit. I told him everything, even the parts I didn't want to."

memory.fact: Zhao Jun told the headman everything, even the parts he did not want to.
Zhao Jun told the headman everything, even the parts he did not want to.

event: "He said you were right to send me. He said the hunt may go, and he'll speak of shares."

memory.fact: Headman Gu said the hunt may go, and he will speak of shares.
Headman Gu said the hunt may go, and he will speak of shares.

event: Then he goes home up the dark track, and Tie Bo goes another way, and the gate shuts.
Auntie Gu waits with a lamp, sets out a late bowl of noodles, and stands over her till she eats.
The east room is warm, the quilt is heavy, and the lattice window is a pale square of night sky.
She sleeps the whole night through without waking once.
She wakes to cocks crowing and a house already at work: water in the yard, a fire in the shed.
Auntie Gu has tea and rice and greens on the table, and Nala eats while the sky outside goes grey.
By the time she is dressed the mist is off the terraces and the sun is over the ridge.
A knock at the gate: Tie Bo, with his bow and a bundle, and mud on his boots from the fields.
He leads her down the lane and out along the channel where the ducks are, to the village's edge.
Granny Hua's place is the last in the west lane: a hut, a garden, herbs hung to dry.

memory.fact: Granny Hua's house is the last in the village's west lane, thatched, with a herb garden and racks.
Granny Hua's house is the last in the village's west lane, thatched, with a herb garden and racks.

event: Bundles of stems and roots hang from the eaves, and the air around the hut smells bitter and green.
An old woman is already out with a hoe: small, square-shouldered, grey hair in a knot.

memory.fact: Granny Hua is small and square-shouldered, with grey hair knotted at the back of her head.
Granny Hua is small and square-shouldered, with grey hair knotted at the back of her head.

event: She looks up, sees Tie Bo, and then sees who walks beside him, and she stops hoeing.
She plants the hoe and comes to the gate and stands, looking Nala over from her feet to her hair.
"You're the one, then," she says. Her voice is dry as husks. "The spirit."
"Every soul in the village has an opinion about you already."

memory.fact: Every soul in Three Stones has an opinion about Nala already.
Every soul in Three Stones has an opinion about Nala already.
Every soul in Three Stones has an opinion about Nala already.

event: "But I'll not take the word of a crowd, and I'll not take Tie Bo's word either."

memory.fact: Granny Hua will not take a crowd's word about a spirit, nor Tie Bo's either.
Granny Hua will not take a crowd's word about a spirit, nor Tie Bo's either.
Granny Hua will not take a crowd's word about a spirit, nor Tie Bo's either.

event: She looks Nala up and down again, taking her time about it.
"But you came in the daylight, and that's something. Not many spirits would."
"Well, honored spirit. Out with it. What do you want with an old herb-woman?"
